**STEP 1 - Scene:** This is a single whole orange (or a large mandarin) on an otherwise empty plate. It is a fruit snack.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** The plate is square with rounded corners, about 24 cm across. Its area is roughly 24 × 24 ≈ 576 cm², so I'll use about 550 cm² to allow for the rounded corners.

**STEP 3 - Items:** The only food is one whole orange, unpeeled.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The orange is about 8 cm in diameter, giving an area of 3.14 × 4² ≈ 50 cm². That is about 9% of the plate, which is the total share covered by food.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** A sphere-like orange 8 cm wide and about 7.5 cm tall has a volume of roughly 4/3 × π × 4 × 4 × 3.75 ≈ 250 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** A whole orange has a density of about 0.85–0.9 g/ml, so 250 ml × 0.88 ≈ 220 g including the peel.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** The edible portion is about 75% of the whole fruit, or about 165 g. At 47 kcal per 100 g, that gives roughly 78 kcal. Expressed per whole-fruit weight, this is about 36 kcal per 100 g.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A large orange typically weighs 180–250 g and provides 70–90 kcal, so these figures are plausible.
